card.name: Linking words before disease or target
card.fires_on: Small linking words and punctuation (on, of, for, since, commas) that come right before a named target, cause or disease, such as 'declared war on' or 'a cure for', in general web prose about health or politics.

modes.label: Prepositions after claim words
modes.description: A preposition after a noun or verb that expects a target, like war, cure or incidence.
modes.example: Thatcher declared war<< on>> the British people themselves.

modes.label: Commas and 'and' in disease lists
modes.description: A comma or 'and' inside a list of diseases, just before the next disease name.
modes.example: This disease affects more Americans than multiple sclerosis<<,>> lupus, lung cancer or ovarian cancer

modes.label: Verbs of effect
modes.description: A verb stating that something prevents or causes a condition, before the condition is named.
modes.example: overwhelming evidence that it<< prevents>> tooth decay

card.plain: It fires on little connecting words just before the model expects a disease or a thing being fought or cured.
